name: @kolu/acp-harness
//exports: ONE door. Everything this package owns is reachable through `startHarness` and the row/state types the contract already declares in `kolu-common/conductor`; a second subpath would be a second way to reach a subprocess, and there is exactly one subprocess.
//scripts: Two lanes. `test:daemon` is every test that spawns a real ACP agent as a detached process group (`src/fixtures/`) — the lane `just test-daemon` runs serially and `just test-unit` skips, the same reason `kolu-omp` declares it. `test:unit` is `src/kolu.test.ts` alone: the kolu reading of a tool call is pure, and spawns nothing.
//dependencies: THE ONE PACKAGE IN THIS TREE THAT RUNS THE PROTOCOL, so the SDK is a RUNTIME dependency here and a type-only one in `@kolu/acp` (`packages/acp/src/manifest.test.ts` holds both halves). `kolu-common` is imported for the row and state TYPES alone — the harness writes that contract and never reaches for a daemon itself. `kolu-mcp` is reached ONLY at its `/fleetRef` leaf, which is the one definition of the `host/id` grammar a kolu call's args are written in; that subpath deliberately carries no MCP SDK and no padi-client, so the manifest above stays true. `@kolu/terminal-vocab` is reached ONLY at its `/terminalId` leaf, for `isTerminalId`: a string the agent wrote becomes a card's terminal only if it passes the same check the wire's row schema applies, so the reading and the encoder cannot disagree. That leaf's one import is effect — the only piece of effect this package's runtime carries.
//devDependencies: `effect` for `src/kolu.test.ts` alone, which encodes readings under the contract's row schema — the check production leaves to the host that publishes the rows.
